static_traits.name: Xia Yilin
static_traits.family_status: Mother is a kindergarten teacher, father is a tax auditor
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; has not yet had similar problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic; rather negative tone, tending to compare with others and negate the positive; able to review experiences and self-reflect, good cooperation but marked self-doubt

basic_info.main_problem: I once won a beauty pageant, but because I only made three friends there I feel the experience was a waste of time and energy, and I have since felt dissatisfied with and demeaning toward my own achievements; this negative feeling has persisted and intensified.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing I tend toward 'disqualifying the positive' and 'mental filtering', which is affecting my self-worth and overall well-being, so I am seeking counseling to change these thought patterns.
growth_experiences: Participated in and won a beauty pageant, which was high-pressure; she originally expected victory to bring marked happiness, elevated self-esteem, and opportunities, but afterward had only made 3 friends and subjectively felt it 'didn't change my life'. Despite receiving judges' and others' praise and affirmation at the time, she kept dwelling on the parts that fell short of expectations, treating positive aspects as 'not counting', and attributing victory to 'luck'. Since then she has long dwelled on negative memories and compared herself with others, believing others are better and more deserving, gradually intensifying dissatisfaction and the experience of demeaning her achievements; she has not yet actively tried concrete methods, nor discussed these feelings with friends.

special_situations.event: Looking back on the experience after winning the pageant, finding she had only made 3 friends, feeling it had not brought the expected 'life-changing'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an important experience hasn't significantly changed my life or brought many connections and opportunities, it isn't real success, and I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly ruminating on negative parts, downplaying or disqualifying positive evidence, to maintain higher, harsher self-standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This was a waste of time; I am not really that good

special_situations.event: When comparing with other contestants, believes others are better and more deserving, and even if he wins he feels it was luck
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are better or more deserving than me, then my success was luck and has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent comparison and self-blame, telling himself he must be better to prove his worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They deserve to win more; I need to be better

special_situations.event: Still feeling disappointed and disqualifying this positive feedback when receiving judges' and others' praise and affirmation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the result hasn't reached the huge change I expected, then any praise or affirmation doesn't count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Actively ignoring or demeaning positive information, emphasizing the unsatisfying parts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These compliments are meaningless; winning was just luck

special_situations.event: Spending a long time after the competition recalling race pressure and feelings of unmet expectations, staying focused on the negative
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel disappointed and dissatisfied, it means the event itself has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining focus on negative details through rumination, avoiding discussing with others to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This experience is utterly meaningless to me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition through achievement, elevating self-worth and opening more opportunities
core_conflict.fear: Fearing I am not good enough, and that my success won't be recognized or will be seen as luck, thus being negated
defense_goal: Maintaining high standards and self-criticism to avoid facing the anxiety of disappointment and being negated
Maintaining the controllability of my self-narrative by disqualifying positive feedback

object_relations.object_representation: More excellent, picky judges or others more deserving of success

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to identify and acknowledge positive gains from the competition or suggests small-step actions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe these positives 'don't count', and that only achievements bringing huge change have value (internalizing external harsh judgment as personal standards)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding to her standards in a gentle, non-confrontational tone, first empathizing with the disappointment, then inviting concretization of standards and evidence; using open-ended questions, guiding her to connect emotions with actual experience, avoiding directly negating her views.

manifestations: Seeing winning the pageant as a 'didn't change my life' experience, feeling it a waste of time
Disqualifying praise and affirmation as 'not counting'
Continuously measuring value by high expectations, hard to experience a sense of meaning

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'success must bring huge change' as an absolute standard
Internalizing others' judgment as self-demands, disqualifying positive gains from the competition

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently comparing with others and devaluing oneself
Finds it hard to allow himself to acknowledge small progress and positive experiences

positive_force: Has won a beauty pageant and received praise from judges and others (objective achievement and positive feedback)
Learned self-presentation and public speaking skills from the competition and feels more confident
Willing to consider joining clubs or groups to use one's own strengths
Having a few friends to talk with (though not yet discussing this issue)
negative_force: Cognitive habits of disqualifying the positive and mental filtering
Frequent comparing of oneself with others leads to self-deprecation
Rigid all-or-nothing success standards (success must 'change my life')
Persistently ruminating on negative experiences without yet actively seeking support or concrete methods

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly filtering out the positive and disqualifying own achievements, accompanied by self-deprecation and comparison with others
antecedent: Comparing with other competitors or peers
When receiving praise from others or affirmation from judges
Thinking that the competition didn't bring 'life-changing' opportunities and connections
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized all-or-nothing success standards and reliance on external validation; when expectations went unmet, using emotional reasoning and disqualifying the positive to maintain self-interpretation and a sense of control
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertain self-worth and disappointment, gaining psychological control and safety through raising standards and harsh self-criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Self-worth damaged, long-term dissatisfaction and exhaustion, difficulty initiating action (e.g. feeling unable to start toward new goals)
